title: "5.5 Performance"
order: 5

Every figure on this page names the population it was measured on. Unless stated
otherwise, that is the held-out {{< var adj.test_share >}} of applicants:
{{< var adj.n_test >}} rows the model never saw while it was fitted, and the same rows as
the scorecard's held-out split ([5.2](data.qmd#split-and-seed)). Two things are measured,
and they are not the same: the **model's PD** (discrimination, calibration) and the
**decisions** the policy layer makes from it (outcomes by decision, reasons).

## Discrimination {#adj-discrimination}

| Measure | Held-out applicants |
|---|---|
| AUC | {{< var adj.auc >}} |
| AUC, bootstrap 95% interval | {{< var adj.auc_ci_lo >}} – {{< var adj.auc_ci_hi >}} |
| Lift, riskiest {{< var adj.lift_top_share >}} by PD | {{< var adj.lift >}}× |
| Gates ([5.9](gate.qmd)) | AUC ≥ {{< var adj.gate_auc >}} — met; lift ≥ {{< var adj.gate_lift >}}× — met |

The interval comes from {{< var score.bootstrap_n >}} bootstrap resamples of the held-out
rows, drawn with the platform seed, exactly as D4's (`wiki/facts/adj_facts.py`). Its
half-width, ±{{< var adj.auc_ci_half >}}, is the precision of any AUC quoted for this model
on this sample. The lower end of the interval sits just above the AUC gate: the gate is met,
with little room.

Lift is the default rate among the riskiest {{< var adj.lift_top_share >}} of files, ranked
by PD, over the default rate of all of them. It asks a narrower question than AUC — does the
model put the defaulters at the top? — and it is the one closer to how the PD is used, since
the Decline zone is the top of the ranking. The function that computes it is named
`top_ventile_lift`, but it measures the top {{< var adj.lift_top_share >}}, not a ventile:
finding 5 ([5.7](limitations.qmd)).

### By population

{{< include ../../_generated/adj-populations.md >}}

On the held-out booked, the AUC is {{< var adj.pop.booked.auc >}}: **below the
{{< var adj.gate_auc >}} AUC gate value**, while lift, at {{< var adj.pop.booked.lift >}}×,
still clears its gate. As in D4, much of the AUC over all applicants comes from separating
the obvious rejections from the obvious approvals; among the loans the bank booked, the
remaining differences are harder to rank. That is finding 1 ([5.7](limitations.qmd)).

### Benchmark: the scorecard it consumes

| Model | Held-out applicants | Held-out booked | Held-out rejected |
|---|---|---|---|
| Business Credit Score (D4) | {{< var score.pop.everyone.auc >}} | {{< var score.pop.booked.auc >}} | {{< var score.pop.rejected.auc >}} |
| Adjudication, LightGBM | {{< var adj.pop.everyone.auc >}} | {{< var adj.pop.booked.auc >}} | {{< var adj.pop.rejected.auc >}} |

AUC, same rows in each column. The LightGBM is slightly below the scorecard in every
population — by less than the interval half-width, so no detectable difference, and in
particular no gain from the richer model ([5.3](methodology.qmd#adj-why-lightgbm)).

### The ceiling

Because the data are generated, the best AUC any model could reach on these held-out rows is
known: {{< var ceiling.signal_holdout >}}, from ranking by the generator's noise-free default
logit (D4.5). The scorecard sits indistinguishably close to it; the LightGBM is a little
further below. A better learner has little left to find on this data: the rest of the
distance to a perfect ranking is the generator's noise.

## Calibration by PD zone {#adj-calibration}

The PD's job in the decision is to place a file in a zone, so calibration is measured by
zone: for the files whose PD alone puts them in each zone — before knockouts and overrides —
the observed default rate against the mean predicted PD. As in D4, two populations: all
held-out applicants, and the held-out **booked**, the loans whose outcomes a bank observes.

{{< include ../../_generated/adj-calibration.md >}}

A ratio of 1 means the PD is right on average in that zone; above 1, the model
under-predicts. The tolerance the monitoring plan applies is {{< var monitoring.ratio_lo >}}
to {{< var monitoring.ratio_hi >}}, and a breach counts only on at least
{{< var monitoring.min_band_defaults >}} defaults ([5.8](monitoring.qmd#adj-redevelopment-triggers)),
the same rule as D4's.

**All held-out applicants.** The Refer and Decline zones are inside the tolerance
({{< var adj.zone.everyone.Refer.ratio >}} and {{< var adj.zone.everyone.Decline.ratio >}}).
The Approve zone is not: observed {{< var adj.zone.everyone.Approve.observed >}} against
predicted {{< var adj.zone.everyone.Approve.predicted >}}, a ratio of
{{< var adj.zone.everyone.Approve.ratio >}} on {{< var adj.zone.everyone.Approve.defaults >}}
defaults — above the floor.

**Held-out booked.** The Approve zone under-predicts further: observed
{{< var adj.zone.booked.Approve.observed >}} against predicted
{{< var adj.zone.booked.Approve.predicted >}}, a ratio of
{{< var adj.zone.booked.Approve.ratio >}} on {{< var adj.zone.booked.Approve.defaults >}}
defaults. The Refer zone is inside the tolerance ({{< var adj.zone.booked.Refer.ratio >}}).
The Decline zone over-predicts: {{< var adj.zone.booked.Decline.ratio >}}, on
{{< var adj.zone.booked.Decline.defaults >}} defaults among
{{< var adj.zone.booked.Decline.n >}} booked files. That is the selection effect D4 sees in
its band D: booking was drawn from the true PD, so the booked files the model puts in its
Decline zone are the ones whose true risk was lower than their PD says.

All three breaches rest on at least the floor's {{< var monitoring.min_band_defaults >}}
defaults, so all three count, and together they are finding 3 ([5.7](limitations.qmd)).
The one that matters is the Approve zone: it is where the bank lends without a person
looking, and there the PD is too low on both populations. No zone misses the tolerance on
fewer defaults than the floor, so there is no calibration observation below it.

## Decisions and outcomes {#adj-decisions-and-outcomes}

The decisions, after knockouts and overrides, with the outcomes the generator gives every
applicant:

{{< include ../../_generated/adj-decisions.md >}}

**The decisions rank.** In every population the observed default rate rises from Approve
to Refer to Decline: on all held-out applicants from {{< var adj.dec.everyone.Approve.dr >}}
to {{< var adj.dec.everyone.Refer.dr >}} to {{< var adj.dec.everyone.Decline.dr >}}.

**The booked include files this model would decline.** Of the
{{< var adj.pop.booked.n >}} held-out booked applicants, {{< var adj.dec.booked.Decline.n >}}
({{< var adj.dec.booked.Decline.share >}}) are Declines here, with an observed default rate
of {{< var adj.dec.booked.Decline.dr >}} against {{< var adj.pop.booked.dr >}} for the booked
as a whole. The booking was the generator's, not this model's
([5.1](purpose.qmd#the-population-it-is-for)); on a real book, these are the loans a new
adjudication policy would stop making, and their default rate is the case for it.

**Approvals default more than the PD says.** Among held-out booked Approvals, the observed
default rate is {{< var adj.dec.booked.Approve.dr >}} against a mean model PD of
{{< var adj.dec.booked.Approve.pd >}} — the decision-level view of finding 3.

## Agreement with the scorecard's zone

Applying the PD-zone rule to the scorecard's PD instead of the LightGBM's
([5.3](methodology.qmd#alternative-considered-pd-zones-on-the-scorecards-pd)) moves
{{< var adj.score_zone.differ.n >}} held-out files ({{< var adj.score_zone.differ.share >}})
into a different zone, and {{< var adj.score_zone.opposite.n >}} between Approve and Decline.
Every disagreement is one zone apart: the two PDs agree on which files are clearly safe and
which clearly risky, and differ only at the edges of the Refer zone.

## Reasons among Declines {#adj-reasons-among-declines}

What a declined applicant would be told. Over the {{< var adj.decline.n >}} held-out
Declines:

| Reason source | Most frequent | Second | Third |
|---|---|---|---|
| Rule hits | {{< var adj.decline.rule1.reason >}}: {{< var adj.decline.rule1.n >}} ({{< var adj.decline.rule1.share >}}) | {{< var adj.decline.rule2.reason >}}: {{< var adj.decline.rule2.n >}} ({{< var adj.decline.rule2.share >}}) | {{< var adj.decline.rule3.reason >}}: {{< var adj.decline.rule3.n >}} ({{< var adj.decline.rule3.share >}}) |
| SHAP, among each file's top three adverse | {{< var adj.decline.shap1.feature >}}: {{< var adj.decline.shap1.n >}} ({{< var adj.decline.shap1.share >}}) | {{< var adj.decline.shap2.feature >}}: {{< var adj.decline.shap2.n >}} ({{< var adj.decline.shap2.share >}}) | {{< var adj.decline.shap3.feature >}}: {{< var adj.decline.shap3.n >}} ({{< var adj.decline.shap3.share >}}) |

Counts are files; a file can carry more than one reason, so the shares do not add up.

**Rule reasons.** {{< var adj.decline.rule_share >}} of Declines carry at least one rule hit,
and the same share carry a knockout ([5.3](methodology.qmd#adj-knockouts-dominate)): every
Decline with a reason string has a knockout behind it. The third most frequent string is an
override's, {{< var adj.decline.rule3.reason >}}. By the code's decision order it can sit
on a Decline only beside a knockout: the override fired on an Approve-zone PD, and the
knockout set the decision ([5.3](methodology.qmd#adj-policy-layer)). It is a rule hit, not
the reason for the Decline.

**SHAP reasons.** The two most frequent adverse SHAP features on Declines are the
scorecard's outputs, `pd_score` and `business_score` — one signal in two columns
([5.3](methodology.qmd#adj-reason-codes)) — and the first raw feature, `dscr`, comes a long
way behind. Three things follow:

- **The model's dependency on D4 is direct and heavy.** When the model pushes a file towards
  Decline, it is mostly the score doing the pushing. A defect in the scorecard is a defect in
  these decisions ([D3](../d3-dependencies.qmd)), and D4's own findings travel with it
  ([5.4](assumptions.qmd#adj-reuse-of-the-score)).
- **SHAP reasons are not adverse-action reasons.** "Your score" is not a reason a declined
  applicant can act on, and naming it twice is naming it once. Where a SHAP reason is the
  score, the applicant-facing reasons have to come from the score's own exact reason codes
  (`feature_contributions`, D4.3).
- **Most Declines are explained by a rule first.** With knockouts on
  {{< var adj.decline.knockout_share >}} of them, the rule hit is the primary reason; SHAP
  explains the PD, which decided only the rest.

The SHAP leaning on the score is recorded as an observation in
[5.7](limitations.qmd#adj-observations).

## Stability

No population stability index is computed for adjudication itself. Its inputs are the
generator's columns and the score, whose stability D4 measures (D4.5); and the training and
held-out splits are a random partition of one cross-section, so a PSI between them would
measure sampling noise, not drift. Stability over time is untested here for the same reason
as in D4 (D4 finding 1), and the monitoring plan carries it ([5.8](monitoring.qmd)).
